header.running_head: The Bravery of Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydillaah (RA)

blocks.text: (Who thrives) When the leaping flames of war arrive"
Hadhrat Ali (RA) stepped forward to accept his challenge as he said:

"I am the one whose mother calls a lion
Like the lion of a terrifying jungle
I give the enemy his full measure just like an open scale"
Hadhrat Ali (RA) then swung his sword to deliver a blow that decapitated Marhab's head. This led to the conquest of Khaybar. [^1]

Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) who was the freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates that they marched with Hadhrat Ali (RA) to Khaybar, where Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him ahead with the flag. When Hadhrat Ali (RA) approached one of the fortresses, the people inside came out to fight him. One of the Jews struck Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s shield, causing it to fall from his hand. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then ripped off one of the doors of the fortress and used it as a shield. He kept fighting with it in his hand until Allaah gave victory to the Muslims. He then threw it away. Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) says, "I saw myself with a group of seven others of which I was the eighth. Try as we did to turn that door over, we did not succeed." [^2]

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that during the Battle of Khaybar, Hadhrat Ali (RA) lifted up the door of a fortress, which the Muslims used to climb over the walls. This led to their victory. When the people tried to lift the door afterwards, forty of them were unable to do so. [^3] Another narration states that seventy men had to exert themselves before they were able to put the door back on its place. [^4] Yet another narration from Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samura (RA) states that during the Battle of Khaybar, Hadhrat Ali (RA) lifted up the door of a fortress, which the Muslims used to climb over the walls. This led to their victory. When the people tried to lift the door afterwards, it took forty of them to do so. [^5]
The Bravery of Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydillaah (RA)
Hadhrat Talha (RA) reports that during the Battle of Uhud, he recited the following couplets (which meant):

"We are the protectors of the Ghaalib and Maalik tribes
Fighting in defence of our blessed Rasulullaah ﷺ
Striking people with our swords on the battlefield for him
As we strike the hump of a large-humped camel (when cleaning it after

Muslim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.187). This narration therefore makes it clear that it was Hadhrat Ali (RA) who killed Marhab. A narration from Imaam Ahmad confirms this when it quotes that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "After killing Marhab, I brought his head to Rasulullaah ﷺ." However, Moosa bin Aqaba narrates that it was Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) who killed Marhab. The same has been reported by Muhammad bin Is'haaq and Waaqidi from Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) and others.
The chain of narrators in this narration is flawed and clearly broken.
Bayhaqi and Haakim. The chain of narrators in this narration is weak.
Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.189). The chain of narrators in this narration is also weak.
Ibn Abi Shayba, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.44). The chain of narrators in this narration is reliable.
